original_text: Animal Communications¨Some animals are largely solitary and join with a member of the opposite sex only to reproduce.¨Others pair, bond, and cooperate in raising offspring.¨Societies -Members are organized in a cooperative manner extending beyond sexual or parental behavior¨Communication Behavior¤Communication is an action by a sender that influences the behavior of a receiver¤May be purposeful, but does not have to be
explanation: Animal social structures range from solitary lifestyles, where individuals only interact with the opposite sex to reproduce, to pair bonding, where partners cooperate to raise offspring. Societies are defined as groups whose members are organized in a cooperative manner that extends beyond basic sexual or parental behaviors. Within these groups, communication behavior is defined as an action performed by a sender that influences the behavior of a receiver. The notes emphasize that while communication can be purposeful, it does not necessarily have to be intentional to qualify as communication.

questions.q: How does the text define a society in animal behavior?
opts: Any group of animals of the same species that live in the same geographic area
An organization of members in a cooperative manner extending beyond sexual or parental behavior
A group of organisms that communicate exclusively using chemical pheromones
A pair of mated individuals cooperating to raise their direct offspring
questions.exp: The notes state that societies are where 'Members are organized in a cooperative manner extending beyond sexual or parental behavior.'

questions.q: According to the notes, which of the following is true about communication behavior?
opts: It must always be purposeful and conscious.
It is defined as an action by a sender that influences the behavior of a receiver, and does not have to be purposeful.
It only occurs via auditory signals.
It is limited strictly to members of monogamous pair bonds.
questions.exp: The notes define communication as 'an action by a sender that influences the behavior of a receiver' and note that it 'May be purposeful, but does not have to be.'
